mechanism_narrative: The current level of the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is inversely related to S&P 500 5-day forward returns. A higher FEDFUNDS (current value 5.33) is associated with negative returns due to elevated risk of recession and higher discount rates for equity valuation.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of all instances, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the unemployment rate above 4.5% signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which increases the risk of recession and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances when UNRATE > 4.5, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and industrial production (INDPRO) from the prior month signals a broad-based economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances when HOUST and INDPRO both decline, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS > 5.0% and CPIAUCSL < 315), the S&P 500 produces negative forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to elevated interest rates and reduced liquidity.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 5.0 and CPIAUCSL < 315, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A strong quarterly GDP growth (GDPC1) is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days. The signal is always active and based on the level of the most recent GDP data (as of t-6mo).
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day returns in > 60% of all instances, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A CPIAUCSL above 315 signals strong inflation, which is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days due to market optimism about economic growth and anticipation of monetary tightening followed by rate cuts.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5-day returns in > 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 315, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in employment (PAYEMS) and rise in unemployment (UNRATE) from the prior month signals a deteriorating labor market, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances when PAYEMS < prior and UNRATE > prior, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A supply shock regime (INDPRO below 100) signals a contraction in industrial output, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days due to reduced economic activity and increased recession risk.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of instances when INDPRO < 100, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.
